name: Nader Osama
notes: Author of the January 2018 Alternative Policy Solutions policy paper proposing a comprehensive progressive wealth tax in Egypt.

name: Oxfam International
notes: Published an Egypt-focused MENA briefing that recommends permanent progressive taxes on net wealth.

name: Hassan Heikal
notes: Egyptian business leader who proposed the 2011 one-off global 'Tahrir Square tax' on large net worths.

name: Thomas Piketty
notes: Advocated a progressive wealth tax in public lectures in Cairo in June 2016.

name: Mohamed Saad Abdel Hafiz
notes: Authored a 2020 Mada Masr opinion article urging Egypt's authorities and parliament to enact a wealth tax.

name: Hani Tawfik
notes: Proposed a 2026 Egyptian wealth-tax threshold of EGP 10 million and a rate of 2.5–3%.

name: Hassan El-Sady
notes: In a 2026 interview, called for higher taxes on large fortunes as an alternative revenue source.

name: Kamal Ahmed
notes: An Alexandria parliamentarian (Attarin district, elected as an independent in 2015) who, in the 2018 budget debate, proposed preparing a wealth-tax bill, as in France.

name: Ali Abdel Aal
notes: As Speaker in 2018, asked the finance minister to record the case for applying a wealth tax even once. Elected in 2015 on the For the Love of Egypt coalition list and a member of the Support Egypt bloc, not of a single party.

name: Mostafa Abu Zeid
role: Former Deputy Chair of the Health Affairs Committee
notes: In 2017, as deputy chair of the Health Affairs Committee (listed for the National Movement in the committee line-up of 3 October 2017), proposed a one-off 1% levy on individuals' total wealth to help fund universal health insurance.

name: Mostafa Ragheb
notes: Called in 2016 for Parliament to study a one-off wealth-tax proposal.

name: National Planning Institute
notes: Its 2017 study recommended a one-off tax on net wealth to help repay public debt.

name: Negad El Borai
notes: In a 2020 post reported by Masr360, proposed a one-off 5% levy on bank-account balances above EGP 1 million to respond to the COVID-19 emergency.

name: Gouda Abdel Khalek
notes: Former minister and economist who described a net-wealth tax as a good idea that should be implemented in Egypt.

name: Khaled Abuheif
notes: Investment executive who endorsed a wealth tax provided it is limited to one application in a lifetime.

name: Wael Nahhas
notes: Economist who said Egypt's tax system should include a substantial wealth-tax component.

name: Samih Sawiris
notes: At a 2019 RiseUp conference, proposed a 5% tax on bank-account balances above EGP 1 million and directing its proceeds to public-service projects.
